item.text:
**Triage Result**

The report is consistent with the pinned TensorFlow source. This is most likely an XLA/TF2XLA lowering issue, not a Python API or regular eager kernel issue.

`CheckNumerics` is a real stateful TF op in [array_ops.cc](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/core/ops/array_ops.cc:1387). The normal CPU/GPU kernels scan the tensor and set `InvalidArgumentError` on NaN/Inf in [check_numerics_op.cc](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/core/kernels/check_numerics_op.cc:88), with CPU/GPU kernel registrations at [check_numerics_op.cc](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/core/kernels/check_numerics_op.cc:365). That explains eager and `tf.function(jit_compile=False)` raising.

With `jit_compile=True`, `tf.function` marks the function for XLA compilation via `_XlaMustCompile` in [polymorphic_function.py](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/python/eager/polymorphic_function/polymorphic_function.py:637). The XLA path explicitly treats `Assert`/`CheckNumerics` as elidable/dummy: [compilability_check_util.h](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/jit/compilability_check_util.h:108) says their XLA implementation is a no-op/dummy, and XLA CPU/GPU registrations enable `elide_assert_and_checknumerics` in [xla_cpu_device.cc](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/jit/xla_cpu_device.cc:79) and [xla_gpu_device.cc](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/jit/xla_gpu_device.cc:96).

The direct lowering confirms the silent pass-through: XLA registers `CheckNumerics` through `MlirXlaOpKernel` in [compiler/tf2xla/kernels/check_numerics_op.cc](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/tf2xla/kernels/check_numerics_op.cc:21), and the MLIR TF-to-XLA legalization replaces `TF_CheckNumericsOp` with its input value, with a TODO saying HLO support is missing, in [legalize_tf_patterns.td](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/mlir/tf2xla/transforms/legalize_tf_patterns.td:397). The test fixture expects `return %arg0` for `tf.CheckNumerics` in [legalize-tf.mlir](C:/ew/ar-coordination/benchmarks/workspaces/tensorflow-check-numerics-xla/source-only/repos/tensorflow/tensorflow/compiler/mlir/tf2xla/tests/legalize-tf.mlir:1300).

**Likely Cause**

`tf.debugging.check_numerics` is compiled away under XLA because TensorFlow’s XLA lowering currently models `CheckNumerics` as identity/pass-through. Since no HLO-side runtime error/check is emitted, NaN/Inf values survive and are returned normally.

**Subsystem Boundary**

Ownership likely spans `tf.debugging` surface behavior, core `CheckNumerics` op/kernel semantics, and mainly `compiler/jit` plus `compiler/tf2xla`/MLIR legalization. The actionable fix would be in the XLA lowering/compilation path: either preserve the check with a real XLA-supported runtime assertion/error mechanism, reject `CheckNumerics` in must-compile functions instead of silently eliding it, or move the check outside the compiled region where normal TF kernels can enforce it.
